newsitem.title: INDIA: India govt under fire over police chief transfer.
newsitem.headline: India govt under fire over police chief transfer.

text.p: The Indian government came under pressure on Monday from a coalition ally and opposition parties over its decision to transfer the federal police chief while he was spearheading a criminal investigation into the leader of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's party.

A government spokesman said Joginder Singh, director of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), had been moved to the Home (Interior) Ministry as special secretary after less than a year on the job. No reasons were given.

Singh was overseeing and investigation into a $280-million corruption scandal over alleged misuse of animal welfare funds, in which the chief minister of the state of Bihar and leader of Gujral's Janata Dal , Laloo Prasad Yadav, and 55 others have been indicted.
The opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) said the decision to transfer Singh appeared to have been taken "under pressure."
"It would send a wrong signal," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted the party's vice-president K.L.Sharma as saying.

Singh, who was replaced by special CBI director R.C. Sharma, took charge of the CBI last August and has overseen a string of high-profile investigations into political leaders. But he has been criticised for publicising his probes.
Singh was said to be on his way back to India from a visit to France and could not be reached for comment.
Last August, Singh publicly apologised after the Supreme Court accused him of meeting politicians under investigation.
Supporters of Yadav, who says he is innocent, have threatened to break away from the Janata Dal and boycott organisational elections set for Thursday.
The Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M), a partner in Gujral's 15-party United Front coalition, said the timing of the transfer was unfortunate.
"It is unfortunate that the decision to shift Mr. Singh from the agency was taken in the midst of many ongoing cases," the CPI-M said in a statement.
"Any implication or adverse effect of this move in pursuing cases of corruption in high places and booking culprits will be strongly opposed by CPI-M," it said.
